details.question: F7 is 10 approved stages, but the Build Loop blocks every feat: commit until 'implemented' is marked, which would be a false attestation. How should F7 be structured?
options: A1: Split F7 into sequential sub-features (F7a funnel, F7b presenter, F7c pre-render, ...), each its own Build Loop + PR
A2: Keep one F7 loop and accumulate all 10 stages into one large commit at the end
details.rationale: A1 is the framework-native answer: each stage gets its own gate, audit, PR and green CI, stays reviewable and bisectable, and gives Karl a working presenter he can rehearse with after the first sub-feature instead of after all ten stages.

details.question: UAT-4: gate_passed blocks all commits, but ISSUE-022 says do not close a UAT gate on the agent arm alone
options: A1: mark gate_passed now, record the human arm as outstanding in the session doc
A2: keep the gate open; no commits until Karl runs the human arm
details.rationale: Remediation is complete and verified (230 tests, sanitizers clean). A2 blocks F8c indefinitely, and Karl has asked not to be handed a build until voice works — so the human arm cannot run yet by his own decision.

details.question: CI is red on PR #30 for a governance reason, not a code reason: entering Phase 3 makes check-phase-gate.sh evaluate the Phase 3→4 gate on every PR, and two of its conditions (a penetration test, and a Security + Red Team review manifest) cannot be met until Phase 3 is finished. How should CI treat the next gate's conditions during Phase 3?
options: A1: scope the CI gate check to the gate actually in force (--gate phase_2_to_3) AND set SOIF_PHASE_GATES=warn for the residual attestation warnings
A2: scope only (--gate phase_2_to_3) — leaves CI red on 1 residual attestation warning
A3: change nothing; merge PR #30 with CI red and record the reason in WALK-UNBLOCK-AUDIT.md
details.rationale: The 7 blocking items break down as 6 Phase 3→4 readiness conditions (pen test, review manifest, HANDOFF.md, INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md, release-pipeline TODOs, Phase 3 checklist) plus 1 attestation-warning count (5 open SEV-3s, feature count 10 > cutline 7 — both of which you attested at the 2026-08-09 gate). The script itself provides --gate scoping and prints '[NEXT] ... these belong to the phase_3_to_4 gate and are not counted against it', so scoping is the script's own documented answer, not a bypass. The residual 1 has no attestation path in the script, which is why A2 alone still exits 1. A1 changes only .github/workflows/ci.yml in THIS project — no framework file is touched. Cost of A3: every Phase 3 PR merges against red CI, which destroys the signal for the rest of the walk.
